title: Commission ESXi hosts through SDDC Manager and poll the returned task to a terminal state
scenario: commissionHosts answers 202 with a Task whose status already reads Successful; the client must ignore that and poll getTask until the specification's status enumeration says the work is really terminal.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact token, commission, and poll wire shape, including that every unset optional HostCommissionSpec and TokenCreationSpec member is omitted rather than sent empty.
prompt:
Implement the standard-library-only Java client in the single file `SddcManagerClient.java`. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at release tag `9.0.0.0`, commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. `docs/official_sources.json` records that specification path, the repository commit SHA, and a separate specification source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source, and the 9.1 revision of the same file is not the contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `createToken`, `commissionHosts`, and `getTask`; do not call another route.

Preserve the supplied public API and nested types: `new SddcManagerClient(String baseUrl, Credentials credentials, int pollLimit, long pollIntervalMillis, Sleeper sleeper)`, `CommissionOutcome commissionHosts(List<HostCommission> hosts)`, `Credentials`, `HostCommission`, `CommissionOutcome`, `Sleeper`, `VcfApiException`, `ProtocolException`, `TransportException`, `TaskFailedException`, and `TaskTimeoutException`. Reject every invalid argument before anything reaches the wire. The host list must be non-null and non-empty; each `HostCommissionSpec` must carry a nonblank `fqdn`, `username`, `password`, `storageType`, and `networkPoolId`; `storageType` must be one of the enumerated storage types; `vvolStorageProtocolType` must be an enumerated protocol when `storageType` is `VVOL` and must be absent otherwise; and one commission must not name the same host twice, compared without regard to case.

Sign in with `createToken` as `POST /v1/tokens` and expect exact HTTP 201. The body is a `TokenCreationSpec` object carrying only the members the caller supplied, in specification declaration order: `username`, `password`, `apiKey`, `idToken`. It has exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `Content-Type: application/json`, a fixed UTF-8 content length, no transfer encoding, no query, and no `Authorization` header. `TokenPair.accessToken` must be a nonblank header-safe string; every later request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

Submit the work with `commissionHosts` as `POST /v1/hosts` and expect exact HTTP 202. Its body is a JSON array of `HostCommissionSpec` objects in caller order, each member emitted in specification declaration order: `fqdn`, `username`, `password`, `storageType`, `vvolStorageProtocolType`, `networkPoolId`, `networkPoolName`, `sshThumbprint`, `sslThumbprint`. Omit every member the caller left null completely; never serialize an unset member as `null`, an empty string, or a placeholder, and never invent a member the specification does not define. A member the caller did supply is preserved exactly, including an empty string, and string values use exact JSON escaping.

The 202 only names the task to watch. Its status may already look terminal and must not be believed. Take the task `id` and poll `getTask` as a bodyless `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` at least once, percent-encoding the id into one path segment so that only RFC 3986 unreserved characters survive; the poll carries no query, no body, and no `Content-Type`, and expects exact HTTP 200. Require the JSON media type on every successful response, and treat a polled task whose `id` differs from the accepted one as a protocol error.

Normalize a polled status for decisions by trimming it, uppercasing it invariantly, and replacing spaces with underscores, because the specification spells the same state several ways. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are non-terminal. `SUCCESSFUL`, `COMPLETED_WITH_WARNING`, and `SKIPPED` are successful terminal states. `FAILED` and `CANCELLED` are terminal failures. A normalized status outside those three lists is a `getTask` protocol error. Wait by calling the injected `Sleeper` with the configured interval only between non-terminal polls, never after a terminal response and never after the final permitted poll.

On success return a `CommissionOutcome` holding the task id, the task name and normalized status from the terminal poll, the number of `getTask` polls performed, and the resource ids of the terminal task, which is an empty list when the task reports none. A terminal failure throws `TaskFailedException` exposing the task id, normalized status, and the error code and reference token of the first task error when one is present. Exhausting `pollLimit` without a terminal status throws `TaskTimeoutException` exposing the task id and poll count. Any non-expected HTTP status throws `VcfApiException` carrying the relevant operationId, the actual status, and the response `errorCode` when the body supplies one. Never put a password, an API key, an access token, or a refresh token id in any exception message.

Acceptance: `java TestMain.java`. The protected verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its request log to assert the exact method, raw target, headers, content lengths, and body bytes of every call, the polling sequence, the wait sequence, and the omission of every unset optional member. The mock loads and serves only the three operations named by `docs/contract.json`. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `TestMain.java`, `MockSddcManager.java`, and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
